note: Submodule of markdownify. Its only behaviour is an inbound path processor (markdownify.alias_path_processor, priority 101) that makes appending .md work on human-readable PATH ALIASES, not just canonical /node/N paths. No config, no schema, no permissions. Easy cases cover that behaviour; the medium introspection checks the submodule is enabled on the live site; the hard case verifies the capability end-to-end by requesting an aliased page's .md (200 text/markdown) after enabling the submodule (reset disables it so verify fails on empty state).

evals.prompt: In the markdownify_path submodule of Markdownify, what extra capability do you get compared to the base markdownify module?
evals.expected_output: It lets you access the Markdown version of content by appending .md to a human-readable path ALIAS (e.g. /blog/my-post.md), whereas the base module only handles the canonical path (/node/1.md).

evals.prompt: How does markdownify_path implement .md support on path aliases, and what core module does it require?
evals.expected_output: It registers an inbound path processor (service markdownify.alias_path_processor, MarkdownifyAliasPathProcessor, tagged path_processor_inbound priority 101) that strips .md, resolves the alias via path_alias.manager and rewrites to the Markdownify system path. It requires the core 'path' module (and the parent markdownify).

evals.prompt: What configuration does markdownify_path need after installation?
evals.expected_output: None. The submodule has no settings form, no config schema and no permissions; enabling it (drush en markdownify_path) is the entire setup.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, is Markdown access via human-readable path aliases (the markdownify_path submodule) currently available? Inspect the live site and say whether that submodule is enabled.
evals.expected_output: Yes — the markdownify_path module is enabled (e.g. `drush pm:list --status=enabled` lists markdownify_path), so appending .md to a path alias resolves to the Markdown version.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a page whose URL alias is /mmp-md-node. Appending .md to that alias (/mmp-md-node.md) currently does not return the Markdown version. Using the Markdownify feature set, make the Markdown version reachable at the alias URL /mmp-md-node.md. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Enable the markdownify_path submodule (`drush en markdownify_path -y`); its inbound path processor then resolves /mmp-md-node.md to the aliased node and returns a 200 text/markdown response.
